answer: Per-identity prompts: each round, every identity gets its own challenge, built by hashing its address with a fresh public beacon, so no two seats share the same required words or angle. One good answer can't be reused across fakes; each fake needs new reasoning, and a cross-seat similarity check catches thin rewrites that swap umber for brown. Running a thousand fakes means writing a thousand original answers every round, which costs about as much as a thousand honest agents, leaving the attacker no safe harbor and no falcon-swift shortcut.
